newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - May 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page of its business section on May 16:
WASHINGTON - The Service Employees International Union's new president called off militant tactics in the "Justice for Janitors" campaign in the District and called for cooperation instead.

WASHINGTON - A civil rights group headed by Jesse Jackson has formally challenged Viacom Inc's proposed sale of its four radio stations, saying the media giant reneged on promises made to the government when it bought the stations four years ago.
WASHINGTON - U.S. states and cities rush to impose their own bans and sanctions, angering companies and foreign affairs experts.

WASHINGTON - American Airlines Inc and the Air Line Pilots Association said they had tentatively agreed to a 16-year labour contract guaranteeing that pilots for the carrier's American Eagle subsidiary remain among the best paid in the industry, while clearing the way for American to buy new regional jets.

WASHINGTON - Consumer price inflation remained tame last month as falling food and energy prices offset increases in the cost of apparel, tobacco products and medical care, the Labour Department reported.
